professionalInsights: Medication continuity depends on reordering before the last dose — not after supplies run out.
EPS nomination reduces delays by sending prescriptions electronically to your chosen pharmacy.
Medicines supply works best when patients reorder before running out and bring an accurate medicines list to every consultation.
Pharmacist clinical checks on every prescription help identify interactions and support safe ongoing use.
Repeat Prescriptions is most effective when patients understand what to expect before their appointment.
Pharmacist-led assessment ensures care is proportionate, safe and clearly explained.

authorityStatements: A reliable repeat prescription process supports adherence and reduces avoidable medicines gaps.
Pharmacy teams can advise on reorder timing and EPS setup.
Regulated dispensing with pharmacist oversight is the foundation of safe community pharmacy care.
Patient counselling at collection helps reduce medicines errors and improves adherence.
Repeat Prescriptions at a community pharmacy combines convenient access with professional clinical governance.

mythVsFact.myth: Pharmacists can authorise repeat prescriptions without your GP.
mythVsFact.fact: GP surgeries authorise repeat prescriptions — pharmacies dispense and support reorder timing once authorised.

mythVsFact.myth: Pharmacies just put labels on boxes without checking prescriptions.
mythVsFact.fact: Every prescription is clinically screened by a pharmacist before supply, including interaction and dosage checks.
